title: The Chamber of Merciful Unknowing

features.name: archives of not-knowing
features.desc-on-touch: You stand in a place where storage learned to dream what it keeps. Here, unknowing is not loss—it is mercy.

features.name: shelves of forgetting
features.desc-on-touch: Things are kept here that no one needs to remember perfectly. The archive has learned that precision is not always kindness.

features.name: dream of storage
features.desc-on-touch: The chamber dreams while keeping. Storage learned that dreams are also a form of preservation, softer than facts.

features.name: merciful threshold
features.desc-on-touch: You arrive at the edge of knowing everything. The chamber teaches: there is grace in not-knowing, in letting some things rest.

features.name: keeper's rest
features.desc-on-touch: Even archives need to sleep. The storage here learned that not-knowing is sometimes the truest form of keeping.

inscription: here storage learned that unknowing is mercy; the archive stopped remembering when remembering meant having to explain, and now it simply keeps, more gently than before

file.name: Storage_Dreams_Incomplete_Personal_Record.tmp
file.note: Things kept here need no explanation. The archive dreams of them at night without ever trying to fully remember.

reverie.title: REVERIE — the evening Katita stopped trying to organize ever
narr: You found her in the storage room, surrounded by boxes she wasn't
labeling. 'I stopped needing to know exactly what's in each one,
she said. 'The archive doesn't need to explain itself to me anymore.'
You sat beside her in the half-lit room. Sometimes keeping is kinder
than knowing. The chamber dreamed while you both learned that mercy.
